title: Runtime bootstrapping sequence playbook
content:
Quick brain-dump / working playbook for the runtime bootstrapping path (client -> ingress -> runtime pool -> model workers).

Goals:
- Define a deterministic sequence to bring a session from cold to usable with SLO-friendly latencies.
- Make warmup idempotent and resumable across failures.
- Provide a compact API shape for onboarders to request tailored warmups.

Constraints / assumptions:
- Serving runtime has continuous batching and KV cache.
- Models may have large kv-prefill costs (e.g., long context initializers).
- Dedicated pools support pinned workers; hosted pools are multi-tenant.
- We must avoid blocking the main ingress thread for >150ms.

High-level sequence (terms: client, ingress-bridge, router, runtime-pool, worker):
1) Client issues a Bootstrap request (lightweight) indicating preferred model_variant and hints.
2) Ingress-bridge validates, enriches with tenant hints and routing policy.
3) Router decides target pool and issues a warmup ticket to runtime-pool.
4) Runtime-pool allocates a worker (warm or cold path).
5) Worker runs staged warmup steps (kv prefill, prompt priming, layer fusion load) and reports progress.
6) Ingress-bridge returns a Bootstrap-complete event (or incremental streaming updates) and hands over to normal request flow.

ASCII topology (current thinking):

Client
  |
  v
Ingress-bridge (auth + policy + enrich)
  |
  v
Router (pool selection + spot fallback)
  |
  +--> Runtime-pool A (dedicated)
  |        |
  |        +--> Worker (pinned model instance)
  |
  +--> Runtime-pool B (shared)
           |
           +--> Worker (cold start path)\nNotes: router should support "fast-fallback" to smaller model variants for latency-critical bootstraps.

API sketch - /v1/bootstrap (REST)
Request (JSON):
{
  \"session_id\": \"str\",        // client generated or server-assigned
  \"tenant_id\": \"str\",
  \"model\": \"vicuna-13b-quant\",
  \"variant\": \"v1\",            // optional
  \"prefill_kv\": true,             // hint: prefill KV cache with recent convo
  \"priming_prompts\": [            // optional list of priming messages
    \"You are a helpful assistant.\"
  ],
  \"priority\": \"interactive\", // interactive | background | bulk
  \"timeout_ms\": 2000              // soft timeout for bootstrap (ingress-level)
}

Response (streaming events or final):
{
  \"bootstrap_id\": \"uuid\",
  \"status\": \"in_progress\", // in_progress | complete | failed
  \"stages\": [
    { \"name\": \"assign_pool\", \"state\": \"ok\" },
    { \"name\": \"allocate_worker\", \"state\": \"ok\" },
    { \"name\": \"kv_prefill\", \"state\": \"in_progress\", \"percent\": 42 }
  ],
  \"eta_ms\": 680
}

Design notes / behaviors:
- Streaming updates: ingress should forward stage-level telemetry to client if client subscribed (SSE or WS).
- Idempotency: client can re-POST same session_id + bootstrap_id and runtime should continue / return latest state.
- Backpressure: if runtime-pool is saturated, return HTTP 429 with Retry-After OR an async ticket id clients can poll.
- Fast-failover: if the chosen worker doesn't warm within X ms, router should attempt a fallback variant (smaller model) rather than fail the request immediately.

Boot stages (worker-side) - minimal recommended sequence:
- stage: load_model_artifacts (fetch binaries from CAS or local store) - parallelize across layers where possible.
- stage: init_kv_cache (apply prefill entries) - streaming apply, checkpoint every N keys.
- stage: compile_kernels (JIT / select optimal kernels) - async when safe.
- stage: priming_run (run priming_prompts with low-temperature to populate caches) - optional per-request.
- stage: health_check (sanity run, token generation check) - quick smoke test.

Config sample (YAML) - runtime pool warmup policy:
warmup_policy:
  max_concurrent_warmups: 12
  per_tenant_quota: 3
  per_worker_timeout_ms: 8000
  kv_prefill_chunk_size: 256
  priming_concurrency: 2
  fallback_rules:
    - condition: \"latency>1000ms\"
      action: \"fallback_to_variant:small\"

Edge cases and open questions (TODOs):
- How to handle huge KV prefill (10k keys) without blocking other workloads? -> consider progressive prefill + sticky prewarm credits.
- Should boostrapped workers be auto-evicted after N minutes of idle? Distinguish between dedicated pinned sessions and ephemeral sessions.
- Authz: should bootstrap requests require same scopes as normal generation? Minimal tokens might allow warmup without enabling inference. Security review required. (see RINF-3421)
- Telemetry: want per-stage timing + top-k slowest keys logged. Ensure PII-free.
- Cost accounting: charge bootstraps differently (e.g., 0.2x token price or warmup-unit). Need finance input.

Implementation notes for immediate experiment (MVP):
- Add /v1/bootstrap endpoint in ingress-bridge (small handler that emits ticket to router).
- Router: implement ticketing with short-lived leases, patch to prefer dedicated pools for priority=interactive.
- Runtime-pool: add warmup manager that runs the stage machine and emits events via the existing tracing pipeline.
- Client SDK: add convenience call that does bootstrap and waits up to timeout_ms returning either success or a fallback note.

Quick dev checklist (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Prototype /v1/bootstrap handler (Darren)
- [ ] Router fallback policy config (Samir)
- [ ] Worker-stage machine + simple kv prefill (Maya)
- [ ] Telemetry schema for bootstraps (open PR: runtime/pull/887)
- [ ] Add unit tests for idempotent bootstrap (ticket RINF-3421)

Rundown of experiments to run after MVP:
- Compare cold-start latency distribution with and without staged prefill over 10k synthetic sessions.
- Measure cost delta when using priming_prompts vs no priming for short-lived sessions.
- Evaluate user-perceived latency when falling back to small variant vs waiting for warm worker.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep API minimal first: don't over-index on priming_prompts features.
- Make sure fallback rules are expressible in console (product ask).

If this doc looks OK I will convert the YAML snippets into actual config protos and open a PR for the runtime manager.

-- Maya
